title: NEB Class 12 English — Language Development — 2023
origin: curated NEB-pattern set for class-12 English language development

questions.solution:
(a) Direct speech in the present continuous with 'tomorrow' shifts one step back: She said (that) she was visiting her grandmother the next day. Pronoun I→she, my→her, tomorrow→the next day.
(b) A yes/no question becomes an if/whether clause with statement word order: He asked (me) if/whether I had finished the assignment. The past simple 'did finish' backshifts to past perfect 'had finished'.
questions.question: Rewrite the following in reported speech: (a) She said, "I am visiting my grandmother tomorrow." (b) He asked, "Did you finish the assignment?"

questions.solution: The report receives the action, so the passive is needed: 'The report will have been submitted by the committee by Friday.' The correct choice is the future-perfect passive: will + have + been + past participle.
questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: "The committee ___ the report by Friday." (a) will submit (b) will have submitted (c) will have been submitted by — the report ___ by Friday.

questions.solution:
(a) Cause goes with 'because' in the subordinate clause: The bus skidded off the road because it was icy. (Equivalently: Because the road was icy, the bus skidded off it.)
(b) 'Otherwise' warns of the consequence of not obeying the first clause: Study hard; otherwise, you will fail. (Note the semicolon or full stop before 'otherwise', which is a conjunctive adverb, not a plain conjunction.)
questions.question: Combine each pair into one sentence using the connector in brackets: (a) The road was icy. The bus skidded off it. (because) (b) Study hard. You will fail. (otherwise)

questions.solution:
1. 'Neither of the answers are correct' → 'Neither of the answers IS correct' (neither is singular).
2. 'She is senior than me' → 'She is senior TO me' (senior/junior take 'to', not 'than').
3. 'since five years' → 'FOR five years' (for + duration; since + starting point).
4. 'full with wisdom' → 'full OF wisdom' (the adjective 'full' collocates with 'of').
questions.question: Correct the errors in this paragraph (one per sentence): 'Neither of the answers are correct. She is senior than me. I have been living here since five years. He gave a speech full with wisdom.'
